weather_alert.summary: Red Flag Warning (conditions favorable for rapid wildfire spread) for Boulder County, which covers Boulder, CO and the surrounding area, in effect from noon to 7 PM MDT August 5.
weather_alert.description:
Red Flag Warning issued August 4 at 12:20PM MDT until August 5 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO

The National Weather Service in Denver CO has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from noon to 7 PM MDT Wednesday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 212, 214, 217, and 218.

* TIMING...From noon to 7 PM MDT Wednesday.

* WINDS...West 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Between 7 to 17 percent.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be favorable for rapid fire spread. Avoid
outdoor burning and any activity that may produce a spark and start
a wildfire.

weather_alert.summary: Air Quality Alert for the northern Front Range Urban Corridor — including Boulder County (covering Boulder, CO) along with neighboring Larimer, Weld, Broomfield, Jefferson, Denver, Douglas, and western Adams and Arapahoe Counties, stretching south and east of Boulder — with wildfire smoke and ozone reaching levels unhealthy for sensitive groups.
weather_alert.description:
Air Quality Alert issued August 4 at 9:10AM MDT by NWS Denver CO

The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Action Day for Multiple Pollutants.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Monday August 03 to 400 PM Tuesday August 04

IMPACTS...Action Day for Multiple Pollutants is now in effect for
the Front Range Urban Corridor.  Increasing wildfire smoke will
result in fine particulate concentrations reaching the Unhealthy
for Sensitive Groups category throughout the northern Front Range
region. Additionally, ozone could reach the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups category during the afternoons and evenings.  For
Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Tuesday, August 4, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
in sensitive individuals, aggravation of heart or lung disease and
premature mortality in people with cardiopulmonary disease and
older adults. People with heart or lung disease, older adults, and
children should reduce prolonged or heavy exertion.
